summary: Mount Gleason tower, Angeles NF: county-built 60-foot steel lookout from 1926, dismantled in 1955 for a Nike radar site; no tower remains, cabin walls reported standing in 2021.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower (M8) with an open X-brace steel cab, and a stone cabin for the observer nearby
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1955; no tower remains. A 2021 photo caption shows the lookout cabin's walls still standing.

staffing.status: last named observer in these sources is from 1940

access.note: Reached by Forest Service Road 3N17, which runs past the lower Nike site (now a correctional camp and fire station). Closed for more than a decade after the 2009 Station Fire; reopened to motor traffic in 2021, subject to fire conditions.

visit.trail_note: Summit is about 1.5 miles past the old Nike camp on Road 3N17; the road may not stay open all year.

facts.agency: Los Angeles County Forestry Department built and maintained the tower; U.S. Forest Service furnished the observers

events.note: Built by the Los Angeles County Forestry Department, 60-foot steel tower, $2,046; completed September 25 and dedicated September 29, 1926. Register says 1927.
First co-operative tower between the county and the Angeles National Forest: county maintained the tower, Forest Service furnished observers
Earliest named observer, I.W. Elliot, listed for 1927 to 1932
Fire motorway extended from the Edison road at Little Gleason to the tower
Lightning shattered a tree a few feet from the tower as the lookout climbed a ladder to it; he was stunned
During a recent lightning period the observer detected many fires near the peak, after lightning had knocked out the Pasadena phone circuit
Chuck Callin hired as observer and married at the summit in June 1940
Tower dismantled to make room for radar serving the LA-04 Nike base; register says torn down in the 1950s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says constructed in 1927. Opening notice of September 30, 1926, a 1933 newspaper that says 'In 1926', and the dedication date of September 29, 1926 all point to 1926. Story uses 1926.
Register and newspapers say a 60-foot tower; Angeles Adventures says the tower was 68 ft 4 in overall. Story uses the 60-foot figure.
Register says torn down in the 1950s; Angeles Adventures says dismantled in 1955. Both fit the Nike clearing. Story uses 1955.

notes_for_editor: Brief lacked a built event; 1926 is supported by a dedication date and multiple newspaper items, against the register's 1927. The register's 60-foot figure matches the brief's height_m of 18.3; Angeles Adventures gives 68 ft 4 in overall, unresolved. The summit is on Forest Service land reached by Road 3N17, which passes the lower Nike site, a correctional camp and county fire station; do not direct visitors into those grounds. The Angeles Adventures page carries photo captions with credits (USFS, USC, National Archives) but no license terms, so no photos are recorded. Tower staffing after 1940 is not documented here.
